walkthroughs.body_html: Hughes opens in media res: 'Suddenly he awoke and was running.' Patriotism becomes 'a yellow hare' panicked across a field. Enjambment makes us pant with the soldier; caesuras stop him dead. By the end, 'King, honour, human dignity, etcetera' have collapsed into raw survival.

Tennyson uses dactylic dimeter - 'Half a league, half a league' - to imitate hoofbeats. The refrain 'Rode the six hundred' becomes 'left of six hundred' as men fall. Yet his closing 'Honour the charge they made!' converts catastrophe into glory, showing how poetry can shape memory.

Owen's eight-line stanzas end with the half-line refrain 'But nothing happens.' The poem's enemy is weather, not Germans. Pararhyme ('knive us/nervous') creates discomfort. The closing image of hands fumbling at frozen corpses asks what 'love of God' could mean in such cold.
